Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · School & learning

edit verb

correct and revise a text

also editing, revise, copy-edit, proofread, polish (a text), make corrections

classical

Cic. Att. 2.16 fin.; Quint. 2.2.7 (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. edit (prepare a text for publication)

ēmendō, ēmendāre, ēmendāvī, ēmendātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive

correct, emend (a text)

To free a text of faults (mendum, a slip of the pen): the word for correcting and revising writing and speech, and for editing a text in the scholar’s sense. Also, generally, to put right, reform (a habit, a city).

Other words

  • corrigō, corrigere, corrēxī, corrēctum — correct, set right

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Hor. Ars 438: corrige, sōdēs, hoc; Cic. Att. 2.7.5: mendum (Lewis & Short)

    To straighten, put right a mistake (mendam corrigere, Comen. OP 97, the master at school); of a draft, as the critic in Horace marks line after line.

  • līmō, līmāre, līmāvī, līmātum — polish, give the finishing touches

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Ac. 1.2: quae līmantur ā mē polītius (Lewis & Short)

    Literally to file (līma, a file); of writing, to polish it.

  • retractō, retractāre, retractāvī, retractātum — go over again, revise

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Suet. Aug. 34: lēgēs retractāvit; Plin. Ep. 8.21.6 (Lewis & Short)

    To handle again, rework: a passage of a speech, a book before it goes out.

  • ēdō, ēdere, ēdidī, ēditum — bring out, publish (a book)

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Traupman 260, 308

    Traupman gives it for “edit”, but classically it is to publish, to give a book out to the world; an edition is ēditiō (see version), an editor redāctor (see editor).

Examples

  • corrige, sōdēs, hoc … et hoc

    fix this, please … and thisHor. Ars 438–439

  • quaedam īnstituī, quae līmantur ā mē polītius

    I have begun some things, which I am polishing with more careCic. Ac. 1.2 (Lewis & Short)

  • Quīdam sedent ad mēnsam, et scrībunt; ipse corrigit mendās.

    Some sit at the table and write; the master himself corrects the mistakes.Comen. OP 97

  • legere et ēmendāre

    to proofreadTraupman 366

See also editor, version, correct, comment.
